avalancheActivity.highlights:
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.
The more recent wind slabs represent the main danger.
avalancheActivity.comment:
The wind slabs can be released by a single winter sport participant in isolated cases in particular on very steep northeast, east and south facing slopes at high altitude. They and to be assessed with care and prudence.
Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher. Single backcountry tourers can release avalanches in some places, including large ones. Backcountry touring and other off-piste activities call for meticulous route selection.

In particular from starting zones at higher altitudes medium-sized natural avalanches must be expected in isolated cases. Above approximately 2300 m they can be released in the new snow and wind slab layers. At the base of rock walls and on extremely steep slopes more dry and moist snow slides are possible as the day progresses.

snowpackStructure.comment:
In particular in the northwest 30 to 80 cm of snow has fallen since Saturday above approximately 2000 m.
Above approximately 2200 m there are 60 to 130 cm of snow, and even as much as 190 cm in some localities, especially above approximately 2500 m.
Medium-sized dry slab avalanches have been released especially on very steep slopes.
As a consequence of the occasionally strong northwesterly wind, fresh snow drift accumulations formed at the weekend. The snowpack will be in some cases unstable.
Towards its base, the snowpack is moist, in particular below approximately 2500 m.

tendency.highlights: Evening: Light snowfall to low altitudes. The danger will persist.
